problem: The trap says that writing W = y₁′y₂ − y₁y₂′ is wrong and that 'a sign flip changes every conclusion'. The sign flip does not change any conclusion: zero stays zero and nonzero stays nonzero, so independence verdicts and Abel's formula (written consistently with the chosen convention) are unaffected. Only the sign of the number changes. Calling one order 'correct' is also misleading, since both orders appear in standard textbooks.
fix: Both orders are used in textbooks. This book fixes W = y₁y₂′ − y₁′y₂ and keeps that choice in every step and in Abel's formula W = W₀exp(−∫P dx). A sign flip changes the sign of W but never changes whether W is zero, so it never changes an independence conclusion — just be consistent.
